v1.feedback: The breathing opacity phase is a legitimate liminal gesture — solid-to-glass-to-solid reads as threshold — but it's the only structural change from the parent; the motes are decorative garnish that don't reinforce the concept. A stronger morph would fracture the growth ring itself at the phase boundary, splitting the single loop into two interleaving strands that almost-but-never-reconnect, making liminality geometric rather than just alpha-channel deep. The warm amber rim light is tasteful but the phase light uniform at y=10 washes the whole tower equally — tie its intensity to per-vertex age so the transition visibly climbs the form like a slow tide.

v2.feedback: The liminal concept is embedded in real mechanics — strand bifurcation at an age threshold plus a phase-color tide — but the random 50/50 strand assignment at birth scatters the split rather than producing a visually legible threshold boundary; try assigning strand based on angular position or a height cutoff so the bifurcation reads as a clean spatial seam. Tube radius 0.07 risks making individual strands too thin to parse at default zoom — bump to 0.10–0.12 and consider a slight Fresnel rim on the shader to give the tubes more sculptural presence. The warm-to-cool phase breathing is the strongest liminal signal; lean into it by widening the color distance or adding a subtle emissive pulse at the exact transition front.
